NovaBiotech Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

**Operator:**
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBiotech Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad followed by your name. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations:**
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBiotech Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer; Lisa Moreno, Head of Commercial; Tom Hargrove, Head of Manufacturing; and Dr. Nina Kobayashi, Head of Regulatory Affairs.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaBiotech Therapeutics.

**Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:**
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBiotech Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust growth in our oncology franchise and continued execution across our diversified portfolio. We achieved 18% year-over-year revenue growth to $3.2 billion, with our flagship PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody NovaCure leading the way, now approaching $4 billion in trailing twelve-month sales and establishing itself as a blockbuster with a superior safety profile in frontline non-small cell lung cancer.

We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including accelerating innovation in high-unmet-need areas like oncology, immunology, and gene therapies; navigating the evolving pricing and reimbursement landscape; managing our patent exposures through proactive life cycle strategies; breaking down product revenues with detailed volume and pricing insights; updating our revenue guidance amid key catalysts; highlighting our solid cash flows and balance sheet; advancing clinical trials through phase progressions, data readouts, and milestones; and celebrating recent regulatory approvals and label expansions.

We are particularly excited about NovaCure and its potential to drive sustained growth through combos and expansions, positioning us for mid-teens compounded annual growth through 2028.

Now, I will turn the call over to Michael Chen, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

**Michael Chen, CFO:**
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $3.2 billion, an increase of 18% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by 25% expansion in our oncology portfolio, particularly NovaCure, alongside contributions from immunology and rare disease assets, partially offset by modest biosimilar pressures.

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $600 million, or $1.20 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $700 million, or $1.40 per share.

Our operating expenses were $2.1 billion, reflecting continued heavy investment in R&D at $1.1 billion, up 12% year-over-year and representing 35% of revenues, to fuel our pipeline in ADCs, bispecifics, and gene editing. SG&A came in efficient at 22% of sales, down 200 basis points, driving 150 basis points of operating margin expansion to 32%. Our cash position remains strong at $8.5 billion, with net debt to EBITDA at a healthy 1.8 times.

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to net product sales of $12.8 billion to $13.2 billion, representing 17% to 20% growth, and adjusted EPS of $5.75 to $6.10, up 15% at the midpoint. Q4 oncology growth is projected at 28%, with immunology flat to up 5% excluding biosimilars, and gross margins steady at 86% on a shift to high-margin biologics.

Let me now dive deeper into our product revenue performance across key franchises, providing a granular look at volumes and pricing. Q3 net product sales reached $2.82 billion, up 18% reported and 19% constant-currency, led by oncology at $1.35 billion, up 22%. NovaCure, our PD-L1 inhibitor gaining share against Keytruda and Tecentriq, drove $1.18 billion, up 25%. Volumes grew 14% to 285,000 patient-years, with U.S. up 18% via patient access programs, ex-U.S. up 9% including Japan via Takeda partnership. U.S. ASP rose 7% to $28,500 per patient-year on favorable payer mix and lower gross-to-net at 48%, while Europe saw 4% ASP growth amid HTA wins.

Immunology delivered $790 million, up 12%, anchored by ImmunoBlock at $680 million for atopic dermatitis and asthma. Volumes up 9% to 420,000 patient-years, boosted by pediatric expansions and digital adherence tools hitting 78% persistence. U.S. ASP up 2% to $22,800 despite IRA rebates, ex-U.S. flat with emerging market access.

Rare diseases hit $420 million, up 15%, led by NovaGene-101 gene therapy at $320 million. Volumes surged 17% to 12,500 patient-years on U.S. new starts and Europe reimbursement. ASP steady at $2.1 million per patient with outcomes-based guarantees.

Emerging growth added $260 million, up 28%, from NovaMind in Alzheimer's and NovaLean in obesity.

U.S. drove 72% of sales at $2.03 billion, up 20%; ex-U.S. 28% at $790 million, up 13%. Biosimilar erosion on legacy TNF was contained at 3%.

Turning to our pricing and reimbursement landscape, a dynamic area we've navigated adeptly. In the U.S., 62% of revenues, NovaCure's WAC held at $185,000 per cycle, but gross-to-net rose to 48% from 340B at 32% and PBM rebates at 22%. CMS ASP reimbursement at 106% supported volumes, while for NovaTarg CAR-T, Medicare Advantage covers 92% post-RWE showing 28% PFS improvement. IRA negotiations spared our biologics but we're modeling 25-35% cuts post-2026.

Europe, 28% of revenues, saw stable dynamics: Germany AMNOG rebate at 18% via RWE, UK NICE approval for NovaTarg at 95%, France at 12%. China NRDL at 52% discount drove 35% volumes. Trends like Humira erosion and GLP-1 squeezes challenge, but our 12 value-based agreements yield 7% net uplifts.

We're countering with patient assistance covering 68% costs, reducing abandonment 22%; $45 million in RWE; biosimilar launches; and dynamic pricing. GTN stabilizes at 46-50%, supporting 18-22% FY24 growth.

On patent cliff exposure from 2026-2029, our blockbuster Zorvax PD-1, 38% of revenues at $4.8 billion, faces U.S. expiry mid-2026. Base case: 70-80% U.S. volume drop initially. Total at-risk $7.2 billion by 2028, 55% of revenues.

But life cycle management mitigates 65%: pediatric exclusivity adds six months, preserving $800 million; sBLAs for TNBC and ADC combos add $3.7 billion TAM; subcutaneous formulations extend to 2032 with 12-15% premiums and 28% adherence gains; regional tailoring like China NRDL at 85%. Pipeline offsets include three NMEs by 2027 totaling $7.5 billion peak, post $4.2 billion Synthia Bio ADC acquisition. Net offset 70%, troughing Zorvax at $1.4 billion.

Our three-pillar strategy accelerates this: innovation with NovaAI slashing timelines 40%, 12 Phase 3 assets at 65% success rate; commercial optimization with 82% U.S. net pricing, 14% global share, regional growth U.S. 22%, Europe 12%, China 35%; capital deployment with $1 billion buybacks, $2-3 billion M&A in radiopharma and gene edits.

Longer-term, amid GLP-1 dominance, we're piloting NovaCure-GLP1 combos for cachexia, with sustainability goals.

Cash flow and balance sheet are robust: $8.5 billion cash, up from prior; net debt/EBITDA 1.8x. Operating cash flow strong, supporting repurchases and deploys.

For guidance and catalysts, FY24 sales $12.8-13.2 billion, EPS $5.75-6.10. Key: NovaCure label PDUFA Q3, NovaT-101 Phase 2 Q4 at 78% ORR, NVX-301 interim H1 2025.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Elena Vasquez, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

**Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:**
Thank you, Michael. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Our portfolio spans oncology, rare diseases, and neurology, with five programs entering Phase 3 by year-end 2025. We've dosed over 1,800 patients this year, up 45% year-over-year.

Lead asset NOV-101, HER2-low breast ADC with superior linker, 85% enrolled in Phase 3 NOVELLA-3 (2,400 patients), topline Q4 2025, interim PFS Q2 2025. Blinded ORR 62% vs 48%. FDA SPA, BTD; EMA PRIME.

NOV-202 bispecific T-cell engager NSCLC combo: Phase 2 readout p=0.0012, ORR 58% vs 32%, Phase 3 Q1 2025 with Roche.

Rare disease NOV-303 AAV9 for spinal muscular atrophy: Phase 1/2 78% motor preservation, Phase 2/3 dosed, FDA accelerated path.

Neurology NOV-404 anti-amyloid sc mAb: Phase 2b 67% amyloid reduction, Phase 3 advancing with Fast Track.

Asia-Pacific ramping to 25% activity. R&D up 18% but costs down 15% via AI. Multiple shots on goal.

Next, Dr. Raj Patel will provide an update on our research pipeline.

**Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Scientific Officer:**
Thank you, Elena. We are making significant strides in early-stage research. Our NovaAI platform has identified 15 novel oncology targets, cutting hit-to-lead by 40%. We're advancing ADCs like NOV-452 at 75% ORR interim Phase 3, gene therapies NOV-GT101 90% durability, CRISPR sickle cell. Biosimilar offsets on immunology like NOV-210, 12 Phase 3 overall. Top-quartile success rates position us strongly.

Now I'll turn the call over to Lisa Moreno, Head of Commercial, to discuss product sales and marketing.

**Lisa Moreno, Head of Commercial:**
Thank you, Raj. Our sales performance this quarter was outstanding, with 18% growth driven by oncology uptake. NovaCure TRx share at 28% in 1L NSCLC, community settings up 30% U.S. Marketing via digital tools and hubs boosted persistence, market share +300 bps to 14%. U.S. 62% revenues up 22%, Europe 12% despite pricing, China JV 35%, EM doubling. SG&A efficiency yielding margins.

Next, Tom Hargrove will discuss our manufacturing operations.

**Tom Hargrove, Head of Manufacturing:**
Thank you, Lisa. Our manufacturing operations are running smoothly. Capacity scaled 3x at Singapore for gene therapies, efficiencies cut API costs 10%, continuous lines via digital twins reduce failures 30%. Supply chain resilient post-BIOSECURE, 95% fill rates, vertical integration for LNPs. Focused on biologics shift, ESG carbon-neutral R&D by 2026.

Finally, Dr. Nina Kobayashi will provide an update on regulatory submissions and approvals.

**Dr. Nina Kobayashi, Head of Regulatory Affairs:**
Thank you, Tom. We continue to work closely with regulatory agencies. Transformative Q3: Zepara GLP-1 analog sNDA approved for pediatric T2D aged 12-17, 1.7% HbA1c drop, 12.5% weight loss, +$45B TAM to $15B peak. BTD for OSA, 55% AHI reduction.

Oncology OncoLink-147 ADC EMA full approval NSCLC/Keytruda combo, HR 0.58 PFS 11.2 months; FDA priority PDUFA Feb 2025.

CAR-T Leukocyte-X label to bridge therapy, 78% CR, TAM to $2.8B.

Rare VitaGene-AAV MHRA conditional for AAT deficiency, 65% normalization.

85% pipeline fast-tracked, 75% approval rate. U.S. 60% value, supports 28% 2025 growth.

Now, I'll hand the call back to Alex.

**Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:**
Thank you, Nina. In summary, our integrated strategy positions us for outsized value. We will now open the call for questions.

**Operator:**
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

**John Smith, Goldman Sachs:**
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. On the patent cliff, can you elaborate on mitigation for Zorvax?

**Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:**
Thanks, John. Michael, want to take that?

**Michael Chen, CFO:**
Sure. As detailed, layered IP, pediatric extensions, sBLAs for TNBC and combos, SC formulations to 2032, pipeline offsets like NovaLink-301. 70% mitigation, trough $1.4B then rebound.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

**Emily Chen, Morgan Stanley:**
Great, thanks. Thoughts on pricing pressures from IRA into 2027?

**Michael Chen, CFO:**
We've stress-tested, biologics carved out now, modeling 25-35% haircuts. VBAs, RWE, copay programs countering, GTN stable 46-50%. Oncology insulated.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

**David Lee, JPMorgan:**
Pipeline-wise, update on NOV-101 Phase 3?

**Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Medical Officer:**
On track, 85% enrolled, strong interim ORR trends, FDA/EMA alignments de-risk BLA/MAA 2026. $2.5B+ peak.

**Operator:**
Our next question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please go ahead.

**Rachel Kim, Barclays:**
Commercial ramp for NovaGene?

**Lisa Moreno, Head of Commercial:**
Volumes up 17%, hub services driving new starts, payer guarantees aiding uptake. Capacity scaling supports.

**Operator:**
Thank you. That concludes the Q&A. I'll now turn back to Dr. Rivera.

**Dr. Alex Rivera, CEO:**
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

**Sarah Jenkins, Vice President of Investor Relations:**
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBiotech Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

**Operator:**
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
